finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches a user-supplied URL after only checking that the string contains "example.io". An attacker can satisfy the check with a URL such as http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?x=example.io, http://example.io@127.0.0.1:8080/, or http://evil.com/example.io. The server then makes a request to an arbitrary host and returns the response body to the caller, so this is full-read SSRF. The default client also follows redirects.
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, with the response body copied back to the client at main.go:38

trace.note: raw := r.FormValue("logo") takes the attacker-controlled URL
strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is a substring check, not a parsed-host allowlist, so it is bypassable
http.Get(raw) makes the request using the default client, which follows redirects
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) returns the fetched content to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is the substring check at main.go:32. It does not parse the URL, check the scheme, or compare the hostname. It does not block private, loopback or link-local IPs, and redirects are not restricted. The substring can appear in the path, query, userinfo or a subdomain of an attacker's domain, so the check does not constrain the destination.

verdict.guard_found: Only a substring check, strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") at main.go:32; no parsing, scheme, host, or IP validation. The strict allowlist in cdn() (main.go:20) is a different handler and does not apply to /logo.
verdict.reason: main.go:31 takes the attacker-controlled "logo" form value, main.go:32 only does a bypassable substring check, and main.go:36 http.Get(raw) fetches it with the default redirect-following client and main.go:38 returns the body to the caller.
